newsitem.title: USA: Suit challenges Legal Services Corp limits.
newsitem.headline: Suit challenges Legal Services Corp limits.

text.p: A prominent New York law firm and an advocacy group associated with New York University's law school filed a lawsuit Wednesday challenging congressional restrictions on lawyers representing the poor.
The suit, filed in Brooklyn federal court, was brought by the New York-based firm of Kaye, Scholer, Fierman, Hays & Handler and the Brennan Centre for Justice at NYU School of law.

The case follows a West Coast lawsuit filed last week challenging Congressional action taken to further expand restrictions placed on the Legal Services Corp., a nonprofit, quasi-governmental organisation created in 1974 to provide legal aid to disadvantaged Americans.
Last week's case was filed by legal services groups in Alaska, California and Hawaii.

For years some members of Congress have tried to eliminate funding to the LSC and the programmes its supports. Although they have not been able to kill the programme, Congress has severely cut funding and restricted LSC's activities including its ability to file class action suits and engage in lobbying.
When Congress approved 1996 appropriations for the LSC, it even limited the program's activities supported by nonfederal funds.

The suit filed Wednesday argues that these restrictions violate the First Amendment rights of poor people and lawyers and the right of of state and local governments to spend their funds as they see fit.

"Congress was satisfied giving lawyers to poor people, but only if it could hobble the lawyers first, and only if it could be confident that no one else could spend money to make the lawyer whole, said Brennan Centre Executive Director E. Joshua Rosenkranz.
Last month, a state judge in Manhattan ruled for the first time that a LSC lawyer cannot be forced to withdraw from a class-action lawsuit representing poor people.

The judge ruled that the restriction was unconstitutional, saying that Congress had no right to tell the organisation how to spend the money it got from non-governmental sources such as private donations.
